summary: This NBL Round 4 roundup covers several games, including Tasmania's club-record 105-95 win over Sydney, Melbourne United's wins over New Zealand and Illawarra, Adelaide's 89-78 win over Perth, South East Melbourne Phoenix's wins over Adelaide and Brisbane, and a dispute over Dejan Vasiljevic's move from the Kings to the 36ers. Standout performances came from Jordon Crawford, Chris Goulding, Isaac Humphries and Mitch Creek, while coaches discussed what went wrong for the losing sides.
one_line: NBL Round 4 recap: Crawford and Tasmania beat Sydney, Melbourne United win twice, Phoenix beat Adelaide, and Bruton and the Kings argue over Dejan Vasiljevic.
key_facts: Jordon Crawford scored a game-high 32 points, including four straight three-pointers to open the final period and a 14-2 run, as Tasmania JackJumpers beat the Sydney Kings 105-95 at Qudos Bank Arena.

Sydney went 10-of-37 from three-point range against Tasmania and lost Jaylin Galloway (shoulder) and Jonah Bolden (fouled out); Kings coach Mahmoud Abdelfattah said they lost the offensive rebounding battle.

Chris Goulding hit key late threes in his 300th game for Melbourne United, which beat New Zealand Breakers 97-88 at John Cain Arena to improve to 6-1 and notch its ninth consecutive home win over New Zealand.
Zylan Cheatham scored 30 points for the Breakers (1-2); Anthony Lamb had 15 points and five rebounds on his NBL debut as a replacement for injured import Justinian Jessup.

Adelaide 36ers beat Perth Wildcats 89-78, with Isaac Humphries scoring 26 points and eight rebounds, and coach CJ Bruton shortened the rotation to eight players; Perth fell to 2-4 after a third straight loss.
South East Melbourne Phoenix beat Brisbane Bullets 96-73, with Alan Williams scoring 21 points and six rebounds; Brisbane was without Aron Baynes, who is serving a five-game suspension.

Melbourne United beat Illawarra Hawks 101-91 in Wollongong, with Ariel Hukporti scoring 21 points and 10 rebounds; Jo Lual-Acuil returned from a wrist injury and scored 12 points on a minutes restriction.
AJ Johnson, a projected NBA draft lottery pick, hit his first NBL three-pointer for the Hawks.
Phoenix beat Adelaide 102-85 on Thursday, winning the second quarter 28-14; Mitch Creek scored 23 points and the Phoenix rose to 3-3 while Adelaide (1-5) stayed at the bottom of the ladder.
Dejan Vasiljevic, signed by Adelaide from the Sydney Kings 48 hours earlier, scored 17 points on his debut for the 36ers, including 11 in the first quarter.
The Washington Wizards waived Vasiljevic before pre-season training camp, after which the 26-year-old returned to the NBL and signed with the Sixers on Tuesday.
Kings chief executive Chris Pongrass said Sydney was disappointed with how the move was handled; CJ Bruton told Sydney to 'move on' and said 'look after the kid'.
